samples.summary: The "every mutation clears the image selection" rule this change introduces (and states unconditionally in docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md, 'Clearing the selection when text moves under it') is not applied to `undoFn`/`redoFn` or to the table structure APIs (`deleteTable` ~3580, `deleteTableRow` ~3623, `deleteTableColumn` ~3648 and the inserts). These mutate without any preceding keydown that would have hit `imageKeyHandler`'s catch-all — a user can click an image (clicking a toolbar BUTTON is explicitly skipped by `handleImageMouseDown`, so the selection survives) and then press toolbar Undo or a table menu entry. The stale `(blockId, offset)` then names whichever inline slid into that slot: exactly the harm the diff treats as blocking elsewhere (next Delete removes the wrong image; overlay painted on the wrong image). Either these paths should call `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` or the design doc's rule should be narrowed to what is actually enforced.

samples.summary: Scope past the issue: opening `handleImageMouseDown` to read-only. The acceptance criteria require only the Cmd/Ctrl+C image copy and the read-only *text* Copy menu entry ('it always worked'); nothing requires viewers to click-select images. That opening forced the rest of the read-only fan-out here — a `readOnly` ctor flag on `DocCanvas`, a `handles` option on `drawImageSelection`, `readOnly` gates on resize move/commit and hover, and a new public `TextEditor.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse`. The branch's own notes record the resize gates as pinned by no test ('Known coverage gap'), so the change commits the product to a new viewer interaction plus three untested write gates for a capability the issue did not ask for.
samples.evidence: `if (readOnly) return;` removed from handleImageMouseDown; new readOnly gates added at handleImageResizeMouseMove (2475), handleImageResizeMouseUp (2515), handleImageHover (2768).

samples.summary: `sharing.md` §'Docs Package (Read-Only Mode)' is the canonical enumeration of viewer capabilities (it already lists 'Drag selection, Cmd/Ctrl+C copy, and plain-click link open still work' and 'The hidden textarea is not auto-focused on mount'). This change adds two new read-only behaviours — click-selecting an image (border-only overlay, no handles, no resize cursor) and the textarea being focused by that selection — and records them only in `docs-image-editing.md`, leaving the canonical read-only list incomplete and its focus statement now partial. That is the parallel-documentation pattern the repo's design-doc discipline exists to prevent.
searchedFor: reviewed the diff's doc hunks (docs-image-editing.md, docs-context-menu.md, tables/docs-table-copy-paste.md)

samples.summary: Duplicated range traversal. The new cell branch in `getSelectedBlocks()` plus `sliceBlockRange()` re-implements the 'cross-block inside one cell' walk that already exists in `packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts` (`visitRangeSlices`, lines 165-190: same `blockParentMap` lookup, same cell resolution, same first/last offset trimming). The repo keeps one canonical traversal there so read and write paths cannot disagree, and the two already diverge — the model one is header/footer-aware but not nested-table-aware, the new view one the reverse. Reuse was rejected on the nested-table argument, which is defensible, but a fix to cell traversal must now be made twice and each copy keeps a different gap.

The #872 fix resolves cells against `this.getLayout()` (body layout) rather than the context-aware helper used elsewhere in the same class (text-editor.ts:4337, which returns the header/footer layout in those contexts). A styled selection inside a table cell in a header or footer therefore still resolves to nothing and still copies as plain text, so the criterion 'Copying a styled range inside a table cell carries inline styles' holds only for the body. Deliberately deferred per the branch notes, but the criterion is written unqualified and the new `tables/docs-table-copy-paste.md` section does not state the limitation.

Surface inconsistency the change knowingly leaves: the keyboard now offers Copy/Cut for a click-selected image, but the context menu's clipboard group is gated on `getActiveSelection()` (a *text* selection) and `selectImageInline` clears the text range — so right-clicking a selected image offers nothing, and in read-only with no text selection the menu suppresses the native menu too (it returns without opening when every group is empty). Documented as a follow-up; flagged as an incomplete user-facing story for the feature this diff ships.
searchedFor: read the docs-context-menu.tsx hunk (showCopy = hasSelection, hasClipboardGroup)

samples.summary: Layering nit: `DocCanvas` gains a constructor-level `readOnly` field whose only effect is passing `{ handles: false }` to one draw call. The renderer otherwise takes per-render state from the caller (`imageSelectionRect`, `imageResizeHudText`), so a per-render option would keep the permission concept out of the canvas class and avoid a mount-time flag it can never change.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree: `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (editor.ts:1282) is called only at 3197 (insertLink), 3443 (applySpellSuggestion), 3534 (insertTable), 3752 (insertImage), 3833 (insertPageNumber), plus the TextEditor hook at 2330 and the exported `clearImageSelection` at 3777. `undoFn` (2090-2121) and `redoFn` (2122-2153) mutate via docStore.undo/redo + doc.refresh + cursor.moveTo + render with no clear, and the table-structure APIs (deleteTable 3580, insertTableRow 3614, deleteTableRow 3623, insertTableColumn 3639, deleteTableColumn 3648, mergeTableCells 3664, splitTableCell 3677) likewise never touch `selectedImage`. An exhaustive grep of `selectedImage` in editor.ts shows no clear on those paths, and repo-wide the only out-of-module caller of the exported seam is docs-find-bar.tsx:124,133 — the toolbar Undo/Redo (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:272-273) and table context menu (docs-table-context-menu.tsx:171,276) call straight through. So the design doc's unconditional rule (docs-image-editing.md:303-317, "every entry point that can mutate text while an image selection is still live calls it") is broader than what the code enforces. The existing re-validation at editor.ts:2297-2302 and 2320-2323 only heals a stale coordinate that lands on plain text; a coordinate that lands on a *different* image after an undo-induced offset shift still paints the overlay on the wrong image (render lookup at 1900-1902) and lets Delete/copy act on it — the same harm the change treats as blocking elsewhere. No counterexample found in editor.ts, the frontend callers, or any indirect seam.
